title: anywaye SLO burn-rate window catalog
description: The burn-rate window catalog, pinned once, in core, and the same eight numbers for every service in the fleet. A burn-rate alert answers "is this SLO burning its error budget faster than it should?", and the answer needs two numbers: a window over which to measure, and a multiple of the error budget at which the alert fires. The Google SRE workbook's multiwindow, multi-burn-rate scheme supplies both, and the arithmetic behind the first one is the reason this is a schema rather than a comment: **14.4 is 2% of a 28-day budget measured in hours** (0.02 x 720h), and it is not 15. Rounded up, a 15x threshold fires *before* 2% of the budget is gone, so the number would be wrong in the direction that makes the alert late about being late. The four pairs are the workbook's: 5m+1h at 14.4, 30m+6h at 6, 2h+1d at 3, 6h+3d at 1. Each pair spans a fast window and a slow one, so a fast burn pages and a slow one tickets, and the slow half is what stops an outage that never trips the fast window from being invisible for a day. The ORDER is pinned by `prefixItems` and not merely by the list, because the generator consumes these in short/long pairs: a reordered catalog still validates as a set and silently produces four alerts with the wrong pairing. `items: false` says there is no ninth window, so "we added one for this service" is a change to core rather than a per-service override — see docs/slo.md, and note that Sloth accepts `--slo-period-windows-path`, which is precisely the override this schema exists to forbid.

version.description: The Sloth spec version this catalog belongs to. `const`, not a `pattern`, because a catalog that silently changed dialect would be read by a generator expecting the other one and would produce rules nobody has reviewed.

windows.description: Short window then long window, four times over. The fast pair is what a pager reads at 3am and the slow pair is what a ticket reads on Monday, and the factor is the multiple of the whole error budget being consumed per window: 14.4x a 28-day budget in five minutes is 2% in five minutes, which is why the number is 14.4 and not the rounder 15.

window.description: One burn-rate pair member: the window Prometheus measures the error ratio over, and the factor the alert fires at.

A Prometheus range duration. Bounded to m/h/d/w with no compound forms (`1h30m`), because a compound window is legal PromQL and would need a parser to check, and this file is the one a service reads without installing anything.

factor.description: The multiple of the error budget the alert fires at. `exclusiveMinimum`, not `minimum`, so a factor of 0 — an alert that fires when the budget is not being burned at all — cannot validate.
